scope_not_read: data/worklists/*.md (task descriptions withheld deliberately to preserve independence)

sources.quote: Enemy champions within {{tt|700 units|center to edge}} of you become cursed, causing them to receive {{as|12% increased magic damage|magic damage}} from all sources.

{{tip|Immobilize|Immobilizing}} an enemy champion marks them as ''Vulnerable'' for 4 seconds, increasing the damage they take from all sources by 7%. Subsequent immobilizes against a target extend the duration of the effect.

sources.where: docs/math-foundations.md, Section 1.2 (linearity of expectation) and Section 5 audit table
sources.quote: the mitigation operator `x -> x*100/(100+R)` is *linear in raw damage* for a fixed resistance - splitting a 3x100 hit packet into three 100-hit packets, or summing it into one 300 packet, gives the same post-mitigation total.

sources.where: cache-wide uniqueness check over data/items.json, data/runes.json, data/champions.json
sources.quote: Abyssal Mask 'Unmake' is the only effect in the cached corpus that grants a 12% magic-damage-taken amplifier; no rune or champion effect supplies a competing 1.12 factor.

step_1_identify_the_delta.reasoning: 157.8 / 140.9 = 1.11994, and 140.9 x 1.12 = 157.808 -> displays as 157.8. The change is exactly one multiplicative 12% damage-taken layer, applied in the old value and absent in the new.

step_2_attribute_the_factor.uniqueness: S6 - no other cached effect supplies a 12% amplifier, so the changed layer is unambiguously Unmake.

step_3_decompose_the_event.note: Both decompositions below are consistent with the observed pair; the Unmake layer is the only difference either way.
step_3_decompose_the_event.if_event_also_carries_mandate_vulnerable: pre-amp post-mitigation base X: X x 1.07 = 140.9 -> X = 131.7; with Unmake: 131.7 x 1.07 x 1.12 = 157.8

step_4_rule_from_source.restriction_a_damage_type: S1/S2 restrict Unmake to MAGIC damage: 'receive 12% increased magic damage from all sources' / 'take 12% more magic damage'. The trailing phrase 'from all sources' qualifies the SOURCES of that magic damage (any dealer), not the damage TYPES. Physical and true damage taken by a cursed champion are unaffected. Imperial Mandate (S3) is the deliberate contrast in this same scenario: its Vulnerable mark says 'the damage they take from all sources', i.e. every damage type. A scenario named 'mandate_abyssal_curse_roster' is precisely the pairing that separates an all-type 7% amp from a magic-only 12% amp.
step_4_rule_from_source.restriction_b_who_is_cursed: S1 curses 'Enemy champions within 700 units of YOU' - the curse lands on the WEARER'S enemies. It never amplifies damage dealt TO the wearer, and a roster member holding Abyssal Mask does not curse itself. In a multi-participant ('roster') fight this is the second way a naive implementation over-applies the factor.
step_4_rule_from_source.restriction_c_champions_only: S1 says 'Enemy champions' - non-champion targets are never cursed.

independent_computation.step_5_conclusion: The delta is a single Unmake 1.12 layer that the old golden applied to combat/events[23] and the new one does not. Every restriction the cached wiki text places on Unmake (magic damage only; the wearer's enemies only; champions only) can only ever REMOVE the factor from an event that a permissive implementation had amplified - there is no sourced rule that would ADD a 12% magic amplifier to an event legitimately outside the curse. Correcting toward the source therefore moves the leaf DOWN by exactly 1/1.12, which is what 157.8 -> 140.9 is. The value consistent with the cached wiki text is 140.9.

residual_uncertainty.statement: The exported evidence tree (data/ + docs/math-foundations.md) does not contain the golden scenario definition, so the identity of combat/events[23] (its damage type, its dealer, and which roster member holds Abyssal Mask) could not be read directly; data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json contains no Abyssal Mask or Imperial Mandate scenario.
residual_uncertainty.what_would_falsify_this_verdict: If combat/events[23] is MAGIC damage dealt to an enemy champion of the Abyssal Mask wearer, then Unmake does apply and 157.8 would be correct. No wiki-sourced rule in the cache supports removing the factor in that case.
residual_uncertainty.why_the_verdict_still_stands: The scenario name pairs the all-damage-type Mandate amp with the magic-only Abyssal curse in a multi-participant roster - exactly the configuration whose failure mode is over-application of Unmake (wrong damage type, or wrong side of the wearer). The magnitude of the change is a clean single 1.12, i.e. one whole amplifier layer switched off rather than a re-tuned coefficient, which is the signature of an applicability fix rather than a value regression.
